A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ranking-score research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Matching relocated and renumbered content supports a reliable comparison, including the retained CDnet appendix results.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo results and analyses of rankings derived from published classifier performances on 53 CDnet 2014 videos, including optimal beta values and rank correlations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds analyses of CADA-RRE leaderboard performances, including optimal beta values and the effects of changing ranking preferences.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2.2 extends the balanced median-based procedure to unequal precision–recall preferences by weighting squared ranking distances and selecting a corresponding quantile, including endpoint values. The original optimizer and error-ratio heuristic remain unchanged; the alternative crossover formula is algebraically equivalent.

E1.justification: v2 adds a focused CADA-RRE case involving cerebral-aneurysm rupture-risk classification and 16 distinct leaderboard performance pairs. The five distribution families and 53 CDnet videos are retained. Other newly mentioned challenges illustrate applications but are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The comparison scores remain precision, recall, F1, skew-insensitive F1, the F-beta family, and the existing heuristic. F2, emphasized in the new CADA-RRE example, was already evaluated within v1's F-beta curves. Newly cited challenge classifiers supply performances to rank rather than competing ranking methods.

E3.justification: The new CADA-RRE analysis reconstructs normalized confusion matrices from reported scores and selects 16 unique precision–recall pairs from 29 entries, explicitly distinguishing this selection from the official three-method ranking (A.2.4). Existing distribution and CDnet evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a CADA-RRE case study examining the reported collapse of F2 ranking toward recall, a sweep relating preference quantiles to beta (Figure A.2.2), and a worked heuristic example (Figure A.3.64). Existing analyses of class priors and performance distributions remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these analyses. v2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure; the retained correlations and across-video ranges are not newly added uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the existing distribution and CDnet results are unchanged. New CADA-RRE results include 44 inducible rankings, balanced beta approximately 0.426, beta approximately 0.914 for the 80th-percentile preference, and heuristic beta approximately 0.789. These are additional results on new data, not improvements under a retained setting.

T1.justification: A.2.2 adds the unequal-weight objective and endpoint-augmented quantile formulation. A.3.8 supplies reasoning about averaged performances and conditions under which the heuristic selects F1 or skew-insensitive F1. The central geodesic and balanced-optimum arguments are retained; the alternative crossover expression and recalled axioms primarily explain existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: F-beta rankings are meaningful and follow a shortest path, F1 and its skew-insensitive version generally fail to give the balanced ranking compromise, and an optimal beta can be found. Additional examples do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains how unequal priorities differ when applied to score values versus rankings, using CADA-RRE. A.3.8 clarifies the heuristic's background-subtraction origins, lack of a general performance guarantee, and interpretation under fixed versus varying priors. These extend the earlier discussion of its empirical usefulness.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, an O(n²) computation discussion and subsecond runtime claim for 1,000 classifiers, and CADA-RRE reconstruction and selection details. The Wolfram 14.2 code already appears in v1 and remains available in the appendix; its removal from the main-text sentence is not a loss of disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted connections to Kemeny's ranking objectives, attributes the alternative crossover expression to Flach and Kull, and cites work on reference distributions, performance summarization, and CADA. These improve attribution and context without substantially replacing the research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and narrative remain intact. v2 trims wording, shortens case-study headings, incorporates some displayed definitions into prose, and adds appendix explanations of the axioms, computational considerations, CADA-RRE, and the heuristic. This is a bounded expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 3 and Figures A.2.2, A.3.63, and A.3.64, moves Table 1, and merges v1's Figures 4 and 5 into Figure 5. Existing appendix plots are retained. The new Figure 3b contains an inconsistent SIVF beta label, and Figure 3c retains an incorrect equation reference.

improvement.justification: The documented medical example, preference-weighted extension, code-access information, and fuller explanations modestly improve practical usefulness and self-containedness while preserving the existing evidence. Gains are tempered by localized presentation errors: Figure 3b labels SIVF with beta = 9999, inconsistent with A.2.4's priors and the paper's beta-squared = pi-minus/pi-plus identity. The additions do not establish a substantial overhaul of overall quality.
